key_insight: AI rewrites of radiology reports can make text look cleaner while either eroding clinical detail or weakening image-text alignment—sometimes both in different ways.
clinical_relevance: For multimodal medical AI, the biggest risk is not just lost words but training on rewritten reports that no longer match the underlying image as well.
method: 450 chest X-ray reports from the Indiana University dataset
Generated three LLM rewrite types: EHR summarization, standardized rewriting, and teaching case preparation
Measured entity erosion, hedging loss, and BiomedCLIP image-text alignment
evidence_signal: EHR summarization eroded 51.4% of clinical entities and 43.7% of hedging language but only reduced alignment by 2.5%, while standardized/teaching rewrites caused 14.9–16.5% alignment drops.
watch_item: Rare pathology monitoring may miss contamination because no rare-vs-common differences survived correction, suggesting task-level audit is more important than condition-specific checks.
paper_title: The Slop Paradox: How Synthetic Standardization Erodes Clinical Uncertainty and Cross-Modal Alignment in AI-Rewritten Radiology Reports
